original_test_intent: Visually verify OSFP Channel 1 indication for functional, I/O-active and non-functional conditions while preserving the undefined Amber Blink state for engineering disposition.
original_method: A qualified on-site operator identifies the exact CH1 cage/lane group and peer, establishes only owner-approved functional and non-functional conditions, applies bounded CH1 traffic, records LED color/cadence, and restores normal optical-link health.
manual_activity: An on-site operator labels OSFP CH1, executes the approved functional, CH1-I/O and safe non-functional matrix, captures contextual and close video, records Amber Blink as unresolved, and verifies recovery.
required_inputs: Exact OSFP CH1 cage/channel/lane map, module serial/PN/FW and peer endpoint
Definition of functional state including module presence, link, lane, FEC and service health
Safe reproducible non-functional stimulus and recovery that does not damage optics or strand management
Bounded CH1-specific I/O stimulus plus expected green blink frequency/duty and observation time
Amber Solid fault class, assertion timing and expected link/module telemetry
Engineering disposition for undefined Amber Blink by hardware/FW revision
LED legend, viewing/color reference and timestamped evidence standard
Passive CMIS/module/link/FEC/error sources and independent fabric recovery
safety_requirements: Verify CH1 labels, module and peer before any stimulus and do not assume cage numbering from software order
Do not create non-functional state by unapproved optical removal, loopback, transmitter disable, fault injection or power action
Keep laser and ESD safety procedures; do not inspect an exposed optical transmitter
Ensure test traffic is bound to CH1 and cannot silently route through CH2
Do not claim Amber Blink coverage while it remains undefined
Stop on link recovery failure, rising FEC/errors, module alarm, thermal/power anomaly or ambiguous visual target
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact source and CH1 physical/logical topology
Organize owner-approved state/stimulus matrix and direct observation checklist
Collect passive module inventory, CMIS status, lane/link/FEC/error and event evidence before/after
Correlate operator-supplied photos/video with timestamps without replacing visual judgment
Perform no module handling, optical fault, traffic generation, link control, reset, power action, retry or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve CH1 identity and definitions of functional/non-functional state
Approve safe CH1 traffic and fault stimulus plus restoration
Define green cadence, Amber Solid mapping and revision-scoped Amber Blink disposition
Review visual and telemetry evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL CH1 VISUAL REVIEW REQUIRES LANE-SPECIFIC STATE MATRIX AND SAFE FAULT CONTRACT
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the target LED to CH1 cage/lanes/module/peer, record video with a timing and color reference, and align each frame with passive CMIS/link/FEC telemetry for the approved state transitions.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds channel/lane identity, measurable cadence, safe non-functional semantics and restoration proof without replacing direct observation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Telemetry corroborates but cannot prove rendered LED color; CH2 behavior and an undefined Amber Blink state remain separate coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An OSFP module can be present and electrically responsive while one lane group is degraded, and multipath traffic may bypass CH1. Whole-module status alone can therefore make a green LED observation appear valid while the intended channel is not exercised.

project_override_considerations: If the platform exposes one shared module LED rather than a CH1-specific indicator, the owner must define aggregation semantics and whether this row remains independently testable. Undefined Amber Blink may be approved N/A only with revision-scoped authority.
expected_evidence: Approved CH1 cage/lane/module/peer map and functional/non-functional definitions
Safe stimulus, green cadence, Amber Solid mapping and Amber Blink disposition
Timestamped contextual and close photo/video tied to CH1 labels and stimulus timeline
Passive pre/post module/CMIS/link/lane/FEC/error/event evidence and restored service

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently maps green to functional/I/O and amber solid to non-functional. Amber Blink is missing by explicit declaration, which is unresolved coverage rather than a contradictory claim.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The CH1 visual purpose is identifiable and manually executable for defined states after project inputs; undefined Amber Blink is retained for engineering disposition rather than guessed.

review_improvement: Adds OSFP cage/lane/module/peer identity, laser-safe fault boundaries, CH1 traffic proof and lane-level telemetry while preserving human visual ownership and undefined Amber Blink.
independent_technical_reasoning: OSFP packages aggregate multiple electrical and optical lanes, so whole-module presence or a host interface-up flag does not prove that Channel 1 carried the intended traffic. The evidence must bind the visible indicator to CH1 lanes and corroborate it with channel-specific counters; otherwise CH2 or another path can create a plausible but irrelevant state.
